questions.q:
Sodium oxide reacts with water to produce sodium hydroxide. 20.0 g of sodium oxide is dissolved in 500 mL of water. Neglecting the change in volume, the concentration of the resulting NaOH solution is _________ ×10-1M. (Nearest integer)
[Atomic mass : Na=23.0, O=16.0, H=1.0]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Na2O+H2O→2NaOH
According to reaction 2062 mole of Na2O gives 4062 mole of NaOH
so molarity of NaOH solution is =nNaOHVml×1000=4062×1000500=8062=1.29M≈1.3M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Let Vapour pressure of pure A be PAo

Let Vapour pressure of pure B be PBo

Using Raoult's law and Dalton's law:

When XA  = 0.7 & XB  = 0.3Ps = 350⇒ PAo ×0.7 + PBo ×0.3 = 350    ....(i)When XA  = 0.2 & XB = 0.8 Ps = 410⇒ PAo ×0.7 + PBo ×0.3 = 350 ....(ii)Solving (i) and (ii)PAo = 314 mm HgPBo = 434 mm Hg

questions.q:
CO2 gas is bubbled through water during a soft drink manufacturing process at 298 K. If CO2 exerts a partial pressure of 0.835 bar then x m mol of CO2 would dissolve in 0.9 L of water. The value of x is _______. (Nearest integer)

(Henry's law constant for CO2 at 298 K is 1.67×103 bar)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
From Henry's law

Pgas=KH·Xgas

0.835=1.67×103×nCO20.9×100018

nCO2=0.025

Millimoles of CO2=0.025×1000=25

questions.q: The osmotic pressure of a dilute solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>273</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. Osmotic pressure of the same solution at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>283</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><msup><mi>Nm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>.(Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Osmotic pressure can be calculated as,

π=CRT

π is the osmotic pressure

C is the molar concentration of the solute in the solution

R is the universal gas constant

Here given,

 T1=273KT2=283K 

π1=CRT1By putting the values in this equation, we get,7×105=C×R×273CR=7×105273π2=CRT2     =  7×105273×283     =72.56×104Nm−2

Atomic weight: Fe=55.85;S=32.00;O=16.00
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Formula of ppm is as follow-

ppm=weight of soluteweight of solution×106

10=Mass of Fe(ing)100×1000×106
Or mass fe =1g
FeSO4.7H2OM=278
56g in 1 mole
1g-156mole

PPM is a concentration term and its full form is "parts per million" and it also can be expressed as milligrams per liter (mg/L). This measurement is the mass of a chemical or contaminate per unit volume of water.

questions.q:
The vapour pressure of 30% w/v, aqueous solution of glucose is ________ mm Hg at 25∘C.

[Given: The density of 30% w/v, aqueous solution of glucose is 1.2 g cm–3 and vapour pressure of pure water is 24 mm Hg.]

(Molar mass of glucose is 180 g mol–1)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
To calculate the vapour pressure of the 30% (w/v) aqueous solution of glucose, we can use Raoult's law, which states that the vapour pressure of a component in an ideal solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution.

Weight of solution =100×1.2=120 gm

Weight of water =120-30=90 gm

Now using formula

P0-PP=moles of glucosemoles of water

24-PP=301809018=390

24×90-P×90=3 P

⇒P=23.22

questions.q:
A solution containing \(10 \mathrm{~g}\) of an electrolyte \(\mathrm{AB}_2\) in \(100 \mathrm{~g}\) of water boils at \(100.52^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\). The degree of ionization of the electrolyte \((\alpha)\) is _______ \(\times 10^{-1}\). (nearest integer)
[Given : Molar mass of \(\mathrm{AB}_2=200 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{b}}\) (molal boiling point elevation const. of water) \(=0.52 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\), boiling point of water \(=100^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ; \mathrm{AB}_2\) ionises as \(\left.\mathrm{AB}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{A}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{~B}^{-}\right]\)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AB}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{A}^{+2}+2 \mathrm{~B}^{\ominus} \\ & \mathrm{i}=1+(3-1) \alpha \\ & \mathrm{i}=1+2 \alpha \\ & \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}} \mathrm{im} \\ & 0.52=0.52(1+2 \alpha) \frac{\frac{10}{200}}{\frac{100}{1000}} \\ & 1=(1+2 \alpha) \frac{10}{20} \\ & 2=1+2 \alpha \\ & \alpha=0.5\end{aligned}$
Ans. $\alpha=5 \times 10^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Ptotal=P∘hexane. Xhexane+P∘heptane.Xheptane

550=P∘hexane×14+P∘heptane×34     ..(i)

After mixing 1 mole n-heptane

questions.q: Molality of an aqueous solution of urea is \(4.44 \mathrm{~m}\). Mole fraction of urea in solution is \(x \times 10^{-3}\). Value of \(x\) is \(\qquad\) - (Integer answer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Molality of urea is $4.44 \mathrm{~m}$, that means 4.44 moles of urea present in $1000 \mathrm{gm}$ of water.
$\therefore \mathrm{X}_{\text {ura }}=\frac{4.44}{4.44+\frac{1000}{18}}=0.0740$
OR
$\begin{aligned} & 74 \times 10^{-3} \\ & X=74\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The elevation in boiling point for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> molal solution of non-volatile solute <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The depression in freezing point for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> molal solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in the same solvent is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></msub></math> i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
We know that

ΔTb=iKbm1ΔTf=iKfm2

And for non-volatile solute i=1.

ΔTbΔTf=Kb×1 Kf×2⇒36=12=KbKf×12

KbKf=11⇒X=1

If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> are mixed such that the mole fraction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in the mixture is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the mole fraction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> in the vapour phase is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given PA°=90 mmHg, at 25°C

PB=∘15 mmHg

and XA=0.6XB=0.4PT=XAPAo+XBPBo

=(0.6×90)+(0.4×15)

=54+6=60 mm

Now mol fraction of B in the vapour phase

i.e. YB=PBPT=XBPBo60=0.1=1×10-1

therefore: x=1

questions.q:
The elevation of boiling point of 0.10m aqueous CrCl3.xNH3 solution is two times that of 0.05 m aqueous CaCl2 solution. The value of x is …………..
[Assume 100% ionisation of the complex and CaCl2, coordination number of Cr as 6, and that all NH3 molecules are present inside the coordination sphere]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
0.05m aqueous CaCl2 =0.15molal solution of non electrolyte

Since the elevation in boiling point is double so the molality of given solution of complex =0.3m

Hence the complex must be producing three ions in the solution, so its formula =CrNH35ClCl2

SO X=5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given, Molarity= 0.35 M

Moles = Molarity × Volume in litres

=0.35×0.25

No. of moles = Mass/ Molar mass 

Mass = moles ×molar mass

=0.35×0.25×82.02=7.18 g

One mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> are mixed. Assuming that this solution is ideal, the vapour pressure of the mixture is___________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kPa</mi></math>. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo></math>Round of to the Nearest Integer<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>)</mo></math>.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given PA0=21 kPa  ⇒PB0=18 kPa

→ An Ideal solution is prepared by mixing 1 mole A and 2 mole B.

→XA=13 and XB=23

→ According to Raoult's law

PT=XAPA0+XBPB0

⇒  PT=13×21+23×18

⇒  PT=7+12=19 kPa

questions.q:
1.2 mL of acetic acid is dissolved in water to make 2.0 L of solution. The depression in freezing point observed for this strength of acid is 0.0198 °C. The percentage of dissociation of the acid is (Nearest integer) [Given : Density of acetic acid is 1.02 g mL-1 Molar mass of acetic acid is 60 gmol-1
KfH2O=1.85 K kg mol-1]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
M=d×V=1.02×1.2=1.224gm

Moles of acetic acid =0.0204 moles in 2 L

So molality =0.0102 mol/kg

Now ΔTf=i×Kf×m

i=1+α for acetic acid

0.0198=1+α×1.85×0.0102

α=0.04928

≅5%

questions.q:
80 mole percent of MgCl2 is dissociated in aqueous solution. The vapour pressure of 1.0 molal aqueous solution of MgCl2 at 38oC is _____ mm Hg. (Nearest integer)

Given: Vapour pressure of water at 38oC is 50 mm Hg
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
One molal solution means one of solute present in one kg of solvent.

MgCl2⇌Mg2++2Cl-    1                0          01-0.8          0.8       1.6

Hence, overall moles after dissociation =2.6

The relative lowering of vapour pressure

po-pspo=moles of solutemoles of solute+moles of solvent

p°-psp°=2.6100018+2.6

For dilute solution

p°-psp°=2.6100018

p=47.66≃48 mm Hg
